cases.question: How long is a commercial offer valid?
cases.answer: A commercial offer is valid for 30 days from its date.

cases.question: After we sign, how long do your engineers need before the build drawings are ready?
cases.answer: The detailed design, which includes the build drawings, is prepared 3 to 6 weeks after the contract is signed.

cases.question: If something on our plant breaks under warranty, how quickly will you get back to us?
cases.answer: The company replies within 5 working days.

cases.question: Is there one person at your end for our region, or do we deal with a different contact each time?
cases.answer: Each sales region (North, Central and South) has its own project manager. The sales team assigns the manager after the first request, based on the project location.

cases.question: When your people come for the yearly check-up, what do they actually look at?
cases.answer: They look at bolt torque on a sample of connections, coating condition (scratches, white rust and red rust), post and pile movement on ground-mount plants, ballast position on flat roofs, and module clamps.

cases.question: Our membrane is getting on a bit. Should we sort that out before your panels go up?
cases.answer: I can't answer that from the available documents.

cases.question: A different firm put up the racking you sold us. Will you still service it?
cases.answer: Yes, maintenance is offered for any mounting system the company supplied, also when another contractor installed it.

cases.question: Our barn roof is pitched at about 45°. Is that within range for RP-1?
cases.answer: Yes, a roof pitch of 45° is within the range for RP-1 because the roof slope specification for RP-1 is 10° to 60°.

cases.question: Can I use GF-1 on a site 5 km from the sea?
cases.answer: Yes, you can use GF-1 on a site 5 km from the sea, as GF-1 is rated for corrosivity category C4 and is used at sites away from the sea, while GF-2 is used within 10 km of the sea.

cases.question: We're doing a 5 MWp ground-mount plant. How much laydown space should we keep free for your deliveries?
cases.answer: The customer provides a flat, dry storage area of about 200 m² for each MWp of a ground-mount plant. For a 5 MWp plant, this means 200 m² × 5 = 1000 m² of laydown space should be kept free.

cases.question: Which fasteners does RF-2 use, and why those?
cases.answer: RF-2 uses stainless steel A4 fasteners because it is rated for a corrosivity category of C4 and A4 stainless steel resists chlorides from salt better than A2 stainless steel.

cases.question: Our plot borders a fertiliser works. Which ground system would you use, and what protects it from rusting?
cases.answer: GroundFrame GF-2 would be used, and the zinc-magnesium coating protects it from rusting.

cases.question: What do we need to have sorted on our land before your crew turns up to build?
cases.answer: We need to have sorted the land plot boundaries, any existing soil reports, and known underground cables or pipes before our crew turns up to build.

cases.question: What is the maximum wind speed?
cases.answer: The maximum wind speed is 36 m/s for the GroundFrame GF-2 product, 30 m/s for the RoofFlat RF-2 and RoofPitch RP-1, and 28 m/s for the RoofFlat RF-1.

cases.question: How long is the warranty?
cases.answer: The product warranty is 15 years and the installation warranty is 5 years. Both periods start on the date of the handover certificate.

cases.question: What corrosivity category are your systems?
cases.answer: The systems are rated for specific corrosivity categories as listed in the product specifications: GroundFrame GF-1 is rated for C4, GroundFrame GF-2 is rated for C5, RoofFlat RF-1 is rated for C3, RoofFlat RF-2 is rated for C4, RoofPitch RP-1 is rated for C3, and CarportFrame CP-1 is rated for C4.
